name: Free My TV
cost: Free (MIT). The TMDB key for the trending picks is free.
works_with: Google TV and Android TV (Android 8 or newer), LG webOS 3 or newer, Samsung Tizen TVs from 2015 on
short: A fast home screen for your TV with no ads, your own apps up front, and one button to go back to the factory screen.
what: Free My TV replaces your TV's home screen with one that has no sponsored rows or autoplaying promos. It shows the streaming apps you pick on a glass shelf, trending picks from apps you already have, the weather, and a screensaver. On Google TV it becomes the home screen. On LG and Samsung it installs as an app through the TV maker's own Developer Mode, and their home screen stays.
who: Anyone tired of ads on a Google TV, Android TV, LG or Samsung set who is fine turning on developer mode and typing a few commands on a computer. If you never want to touch adb, skip it.
needs: A computer on the same Wi-Fi as the TV
adb, for the ready APK on Google TV and Android TV
Python 3 for LG TVs, and a free LG developer account
A free TMDB key if you want the trending picks

steps.title: Turn on USB debugging on the TV
steps.text: Settings → System → About → press Android TV OS build 7 times. Then Settings → System → Developer options → turn on USB debugging. Write down the TV's IP address.

steps.title: Install the ready APK
steps.text: Download `FreeMyTV.apk` from the latest release and install it with adb, not by opening the APK on the TV. Swap in your TV's IP.

steps.title: Switch it on
steps.text: On the TV, open Free My TV → Home Screen → Free My TV. When the TV asks Allow USB debugging? for Free My TV, tick Always allow and accept.

steps.title: Add your TMDB key
steps.text: In Home Settings → TMDB key, scan the QR code with your phone and paste the key, or type the short API Key with the remote.

steps.title: On an LG TV instead
steps.text: Install Developer Mode from the LG Content Store, turn on Dev Mode Status and Key Server, then build and install from your computer. The first install asks for the TV's passphrase.
steps.code:
git clone https://github.com/simbasjungles/free-my-tv && cd free-my-tv
python3 webos/build.py
python3 webos/install.py 192.168.1.50

steps.title: On a Samsung TV instead
steps.text: Turn on Developer mode (Apps, then `1 2 3 4 5` on the remote) and set Host PC IP. Then open TizenBrew Installer on your computer, connect to the TV and install from GitHub with `simbasjungles/free-my-tv`.

steps.title: To undo it
steps.text: On the TV: Free My TV → Home Screen → Original. The factory home screen, screensaver and every app come back.

try.label: From the README
try.where: An AI coding agent on your computer
try.text: With USB debugging on, ask your agent: "Install Free My TV (github.com/simbasjungles/free-my-tv) on my TV at 192.168.1.50. I live in Lisbon." Swap in your TV's IP and city. It builds the app and asks before anything important.

watch: On Google TV it turns off the stock home screen, the screensaver and some maker apps (without uninstalling them). Picture, sound, inputs, remote pairing and the Play Store are on a protected list.
On Android 14, Google Play Protect may hold the install with Risky app blocked. The README says to choose More details → Install anyway.
It uses an accessibility service for some remote buttons and, only while the Now Playing widget is on, a notification listener. It says it never reads a notification.
No accounts or analytics. It talks to TMDB and Open-Meteo, the release APK checks GitHub for updates once a week, and other services only when you set them up.
The phone page for sending your TMDB key is plain HTTP on your Wi-Fi. On a network you don't trust, type the key instead.
LG Developer Mode lasts about 40 days unless you press EXTEND or run `webos/renew.py`.
